cases: Fresh actor authority rejects all create/update/delete and recovery methods
Creation replay and scoped recovery return one exact lead
Creation cancelled before arrival cannot be replayed; cancellation never deletes existing lead
Changed creation input cannot reuse an operation ID
Deleted creation keeps its receipt and cannot resurrect data
Versioned PATCH rejects stale edit and preserves newest row
Concurrent same-version PATCH has one accepted write under serialized synthetic transactions
Versioned DELETE refuses stale state, then logically deletes only the reviewed row
Missing review version cannot bypass PATCH or DELETE conflict protection
Conversion invariants reject fabricated conversion and converted status rollback
Overlong PATCH fields reject unchanged rather than truncate
Malformed metadata, IDs, version and duplicate version query reject before mutation
Foreign or inactive row is inaccessible for PATCH, DELETE and detail recovery
Receipt persistence failure rolls back manual creation
Import accepts valid rows and explicitly reports skipped missing-name positions
Whole import rejects overlong or malformed optional field without partial insert
Import replay creates one batch and exact recovery checks its owned active row set
Cancelled import blocks late arrival and never deletes committed batch
Unavailable batch and changed input cannot replay or recreate deleted rows
Partial insertion, result marker failure and receipt failure all roll back entire import
Actor and organization isolate manual and batch recovery receipts
All handled errors and successes are private; unknown failures never expose diagnostics
scope: Actual manual create/detail PATCH/DELETE/recovery/import handlers and shared authority/receipt/validation/Serializable admission helpers, synthetic Prisma transactions with rollback and serialized scheduling. Not actual PostgreSQL concurrency, mounted UI or production/customer/provider writes.
